## Observed (RUNNING, this session)

PR #656 merged the capture-health observer wiring in server/main.ts, ledger item 28 supplied the config ruling, and OPENBRAIN_CAPTURE_HEALTH_NAMESPACE=rico sits in /Volumes/ThunderBolt/open-brain-local/local-clone.env (line 65, byte-clean, mtime before boot). The clone was redeployed at 1d2e848 with revision proof PASSED — and live /health publishes NO capture block.

Evidence chain:
- Boot log (autostart.out.log 22:21:35Z): `capture_health_namespace_missing ... capture_health_enabled:false` — the observer's loud-on-absence path, working as designed.
- Launcher process 3067 (`bun run scripts/local-clone.ts --start`): HAS the var in its env (the autostart wrapper sources local-clone.env correctly).
- Server child 3463 (`bun run server/main.ts`): does NOT have it.

## Root cause

`scripts/local-clone.ts` `buildChildEnvironment()` passes the child an ALLOWLIST (`CHILD_ENV_KEYS`) plus two prefix families (`AUTH_TOKEN_USER_*`, `OPENBRAIN_TRACING_*`). `OPENBRAIN_CAPTURE_HEALTH_*` is in neither, so the launcher drops it. This is the third instance of the deploy-coupling class the code itself documents at the #530 tracing comment ("must reach the server child or createTracingRuntime silently stays off").

Two defects here, not one:
1. The three OPENBRAIN_CAPTURE_HEALTH_* keys don't reach the server child.
2. The allowlist violates "nothing is adjusted silently" (repo coding standard, operator ruling 2026-08-08): it drops configured keys without announcing which. Every future server config key re-buys this bug until the drop is announced.

## Done-means design (red-first)

RED against current main: a unit-level check on buildChildEnvironment with OPENBRAIN_CAPTURE_HEALTH_NAMESPACE set in the input env asserts the key in the output — fails today. Plus an announce clause: with a known-unlisted key set, the launcher's output names the dropped key (fails today, silent). Control: DB_*/AUTH_TOKEN_* still pass through; a deliberately-unlisted junk key still does NOT pass (the allowlist stays an allowlist — announced, not abolished). Live GREEN after redeploy: /health publishes the capture block (that step is the controller's, post-merge).

Also worth a clause: done-means 656 clause (b) drove createShadowApplication directly, so this whole launcher seam was outside its vantage — the check measured the composition, not the deployment chain. The lane should say whether a cheap chain-level clause (spawn the launcher's buildChildEnvironment output into the shadow app) is feasible.
